acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year. Stores and online together, one contract.

header.reason: The COO's store team judged the deal on stores. Adyen brought people who had done store rollouts, while we only described the till return, offered a partner for installs and had no rollout plan or reference call. Tom says we had won the web side and had the better online product, but the deal was one contract for stores and online, and nothing shows any part of it came to us.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Holiday buy-online-return-in-store failures and a loyalty launch that broke on split store and web customer records started the evaluation, and the COO watched it happen in a store queue. In this deal, messaging that speaks to the post-holiday returns moment at the till would have hit the real pain.
findings.quote: The store couldn't see the online order, so staff were refunding to gift cards or telling people to mail it back.

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Angela, the COO, signed with Adyen, and her store team asked for the workshop that sank us. Tom worked with Raj, the CTO, as his contact and called him the decider at first. Tom met Angela only once, at kickoff, so our champion was not the person who made the call.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Tom wasn't there. Raj told him afterwards that Adyen came with a retail team who had done store rollouts, pitched one platform for tills and web on one contract, and named retailers Angela knew. After that meeting the customer's questions moved from checkout and wallets to store wifi, rolling out 120 stores and Saturday till outages.
findings.quote: Raj forwarded me a list of 14 questions and 11 of them were about stores.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: The online checkout demo, with wallets and one-click, won over the ecommerce lead. The unified commerce slide claiming 'the line between them has pretty much disappeared' got silence and a dismissal from store operations. Our answer that 'we'd bring in a partner' for installs also ended Bev's questions. Abstract platform claims did not land with the store buyers.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: They asked for three things we never delivered: a reference retailer they could call (we sent a case study instead), a rollout plan with dates, installers and what happens to the old tills, and a live demo of an online order returned at a store till. Here, store proof shown live counted more than written stories.
findings.quote: They wanted to watch an online order get returned at a store till, live. We described it. We never showed it.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: The customer said 'the tills', 'one customer, one basket' and 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other'. We said 'unified commerce', 'in-person payments' and 'point of sale'. Their language was concrete and store-floor, and single-vendor accountability mattered to them, which our partner-install answer cut against.
findings.quote: One system for the tills and the website.
